facts.label: Tax and currency
facts.value: Fees are USD unless invoice/order explicitly says otherwise; published fees exclude applicable taxes, duties, tariffs, and levies.

facts.label: Paid seat and roles
facts.value: A user is a support agent who can be assigned requests and interact with customers. Owner starts as Admin; Admin, Manager, Staff, and Watcher roles exist.

facts.label: Ticket allowances
facts.value: Published cards: Free 100, Essentials 1,000, Business 6,000, Elite starting at 15,000, Suite 60,000 tickets/month.

facts.label: Counting rules
facts.value: Whether reopened tickets, repeat customer messages, spam, imports, merged tickets, or auto-created channel tickets consume new monthly quota was not published in the checked sources.

facts.label: Minimum purchase and optional package
facts.value: Free: one agent. Paid Essentials and Business public checkout show one agent. Elite's explicit minimum bundle is three agents. White Label is an optional paid checkbox.

facts.label: Three-seat entry-plan scope
facts.value: Entry-plan additional-seat purchase route and how its ticket quota scales were not fully established. Per-user arithmetic is available, but a three-seat Essentials checkout total was not confirmed.

facts.label: Renewal and cancellation
facts.value: Auto-renewal; cancel at least 24 hours before term end. Owner can use My Account → Cancel Account; support assists if access fails. Paid access continues to term end.

facts.label: Initial refund and help-page discrepancy
facts.value: Terms section 34 and paid checkout promise a 15-day money-back guarantee on the initial purchase. Cancellation guide broadly says no refunds without explaining that exception.

facts.label: Included AI / Essentials
facts.value: Essentials card includes up to 50 AI-drafted replies/month, ticket categorization, and grammar/spell checking.

facts.label: AI / higher plans
facts.value: Business adds first-response generation and tone rewriting; Elite adds sentiment/emotion and redaction plus an AI-first 15,000-ticket offer; Suite advertises autonomous ticket replies/closure.

facts.label: AI limit discrepancy
facts.value: Essentials pricing says 50 monthly drafts; annual checkout promotes unlimited AI usage limits without a resource definition. Exact scope of the annual entitlement is unresolved.

facts.label: Overage/model rates
facts.value: No Desk-specific AI overage price, model multiplier, per-resolution rate, regeneration counter, or required separate model-provider account found.

facts.label: AI examples / 100 and 500 drafts
facts.value: Exact totals not calculable. Under the explicit 50-draft allowance, 100 drafts need 50 extra and 500 need 450 extra; no extra-draft rate is published. Annual unlimited-AI wording introduces an additional scope ambiguity.

facts.label: White Label add-on
facts.value: USD 300/year with annual purchase or USD 30/month with monthly purchase; removes Powered By links. Optional.

facts.label: Fair use and hard stops
facts.value: Terms may charge extra, suspend, or terminate excessive use despite unlimited feature descriptions. Exact ticket-overage rates, automatic quota upgrades/recharge, and AI hard-stop rules not published in the checked Desk sources.

facts.label: Failed payments and late invoices
facts.value: Terms: up to 3 payment retries over 10 days; then immediate suspension; after 10 suspended days, free downgrade if available or deletion. Overdue invoiced balances can incur 1.5%/month or the lower lawful maximum.

facts.label: Payment-processing fees
facts.value: Visa, Mastercard, AmEx accepted; pricing says no PayPal. Purchases over USD 3,000 may use ACH or cheque with an additional USD 100 processing fee.

facts.label: Attachment limit and channel expenses
facts.value: Ticket response attachments maximum 20 MB at once; create-ticket API also documents a 20 MB maximum. Connected Twilio requires a separate account and active phone number.

facts.label: Branding and email identity
facts.value: Desk customization supports logo, favicon, header linkback URL, and browser-tab title. Agent and inbox-specific email signatures can contain text/images.

facts.label: Attribution-removal package
facts.value: White Label package explicitly removes Powered By links; USD 300/year or USD 30/month in the public paid checkout.

facts.label: Surface-specific removal scope
facts.value: Exact removal coverage for customer portal, outgoing mail, connected Knowledge Base, and connected Chat widget, and free/trial eligibility were not published in the checked sources.

facts.label: Buying access
facts.value: Self-service signup, forever-free single-user offer, and public paid checkout; demo and sales contact also available. Solo access is explicit.

facts.label: Type and fit
facts.value: Our classification: support ticketing and shared inboxes with workflow automation, customer portal, AI assistance, and connected chat/help-content products.

facts.label: Email
facts.value: Native email tickets; forwarding documented for Gmail/G Suite, Google Groups, Yahoo, Outlook, and Microsoft 365. Free includes email ticketing with its 100-ticket cap.

facts.label: Website forms and portal
facts.value: Customer portal lets contacts register/log in, create tickets with attachments, reply, and view open/closed ticket history. Business pricing lists custom website/help-center intake forms.

facts.label: Website live chat
facts.value: ProProfs Chat integration supports creating tickets during chats, attaching transcripts, and converting offline messages to tickets. Elite/Suite pricing explicitly advertises website chat/omnichannel.

facts.label: WhatsApp
facts.value: Direct Help Desk connection to WhatsApp Business number/inbox; creates or updates tickets and sends agent replies back on WhatsApp. Business-app coexistence described.

facts.label: Facebook
facts.value: Documented Facebook Page integration turns the first post comment into a ticket, appends later comments on that post, and posts agent replies back as comments.

facts.label: Instagram and Messenger
facts.value: Elite/Suite marketing advertises Instagram DMs and Facebook Messenger; dedicated private-message setup/permission details not found in the checked Desk guides.

facts.label: SMS
facts.value: Twilio integration converts incoming SMS to tickets and lets agents handle text conversations in Desk.

facts.label: Voice
facts.value: Twilio voice integration documents call handling and call details within Help Desk.

facts.label: Slack / Discord / in-app channels
facts.value: Slack integration is ticket notifications, not documented incoming customer conversations. Native Discord support and a Help Desk customer in-app SDK channel were not established.

facts.label: Lower-plan channel gates
facts.value: Exact first plan and extra subscription requirements for connected Chat/social/telephony on Free, Essentials, and Business remain unresolved.

facts.label: Assignment and roles
facts.value: Ticket assignment, team/inbox access, round-robin assignment to online agents, and max-open-ticket controls are documented.

facts.label: Notes, replies and bulk actions
facts.value: Internal notes, canned replies, ticket priority/labels/status, and bulk ticket organization documented. Business pricing adds merge/bulk operations.

facts.label: Rules and hours
facts.value: Essentials has basic automation; Business smart workflows; Elite smart ticket flow/SLAs. Docs support rules based on intent, sentiment, priority, and inbox plus working shifts/holidays.

facts.label: Collision warnings
facts.value: A specific simultaneous-reply/collision-warning behavior and plan gate were not found in the checked core workflow, settings, pricing, or terms pages.

facts.label: Inboxes and products
facts.value: Free and Business pricing explicitly list unlimited inboxes. Inboxes can have distinct destinations, agent access, email signatures, and portal associations.

facts.label: Multiple portals
facts.value: Multiple customer portals with separate custom domains, names, inbox destinations, branding, and notification settings are documented.

facts.label: Resource maxima
facts.value: Numerical portal/brand limits, number of external stores/numbers permitted per account, and extra-brand prices not published in checked pricing/configuration/terms.

facts.label: Help-content connection
facts.value: Pricing says a Help Desk subscription includes Knowledge Base. Dedicated integration connects a KB URL, syncs articles, and lets agents select default articles from the ticket sidebar.

facts.label: Articles and customer portal
facts.value: Portal setup advertises access to knowledge content; integration guide describes searching/browsing articles and recommending selected articles in replies.

facts.label: Included KB limits and features
facts.value: Exact bundled KB author/site/article/storage allowance, automatic article translation, article-feedback entitlement, and bundled custom-domain/branding tier were not established.

facts.label: Agent-assist AI
facts.value: Generate AI Replies drafts editable responses; Conversational AI summarizes/analyzes ticket history, searches connected sources for help articles, and inserts results into a draft.

facts.label: Autonomous role
facts.value: AI product page advertises reading, prioritizing, resolving, and closing routine tickets autonomously. Suite pricing explicitly describes sending an answer and closing without agent involvement.

facts.label: AI sources
facts.value: Knowledge Base, public website URLs, uploaded documents, and past resolved tickets. Past Tickets has an enable toggle; KB uses account/product connection.

facts.label: AI source limits
facts.value: Uploaded .txt, .doc, .docx, or .pdf, up to 10 MB/file. Private/login-protected URLs cannot be processed. Website crawl controls include maximum depth and maximum pages.

facts.label: Refresh and evidence controls
facts.value: Exact automatic resync interval, update latency, per-answer citation guarantee, and a source-change approval workflow were not published in the checked docs/pricing/terms.

facts.label: Human response and history
facts.value: Agent-assist output remains in the ticket/editor for review. Chat-to-ticket integration can attach the transcript; offline Chat messages automatically become tickets.

facts.label: Offline and AI handoff
facts.value: Connected Chat pricing lets the owner hide chat, collect offline messages, or use AI when operators are offline; its agent handoff claim includes bot context. Desk marketing says humans handle escalations.

facts.label: Human Shopify actions
facts.value: Shopify integration documents viewing orders/products, editing shipping details, cancellation, and full/partial refunds from Desk's order panel.

facts.label: Autonomous actions and verification
facts.value: Suite marketing names creating CRM leads/tickets, follow-up emails, and triggering workflows through agentic Chat. A Desk-specific autonomous refund/order-change authorization or customer identity-check workflow was not found.

facts.label: Shopify and BigCommerce
facts.value: Dedicated commerce integrations documented; Shopify supplies order context and agent order actions; BigCommerce appears in the official integration directory.

facts.label: Slack and work tools
facts.value: Slack sends ticket notifications to a chosen channel; official directory lists Jira and ClickUp ticket/task connections, Salesforce, HubSpot, Asana, and ProProfs Project.

facts.label: Remaining requested connections
facts.value: Native WooCommerce, Stripe, Discord, Linear, GitHub, and a specific Zapier/Make route not found in the checked integration directory and developer docs.

facts.label: Public API
facts.value: Documented REST endpoints create/update tickets, retrieve ticket lists, and create company/contact records; uses account email plus API token and JSON.

facts.label: Webhooks
facts.value: Create-ticket and reply events; selectable ticket fields; JSON payload, URL-verification challenge, and a test facility documented.

facts.label: Plan and technical limits
facts.value: Free feature area lists API/SSO; Elite specifically lists full API/webhooks. Endpoint-by-endpoint lower-plan gates, request-rate limits, retry schedule, and native customer SDK limits were not published in checked sources.

facts.label: Self-hosting
facts.value: Not applicable to the proprietary vendor-hosted edition researched.

facts.label: Language coverage
facts.value: Complete named lists for Desk agent UI, customer portal/forms, bundled articles, and Desk AI answer languages were not found.

facts.label: Platforms and devices
facts.value: Browser-based Desk; current pricing advertises agent mobile support and Elite's native iOS/Android app. No mandatory WordPress, Shopify, Gmail, or macOS host platform for the core help desk.

facts.label: Reporting
facts.value: Summary, rating, custom fields, users, child tickets, labels, scheduled reports, company/contact, overdue, and ticket export reports documented.

facts.label: AI review
facts.value: Conversational AI analyzes ticket history; autonomous product marketing advertises recurring-issue and performance insights. No published standardized failed-AI-answer metric or guaranteed resolution-accuracy score found.

facts.label: Spreadsheet ticket export
facts.value: Agent interface can download tickets in Excel-sheet format; Reports → Export Tickets supports filters such as dates, inbox, and user. General settings can disable ticket downloading.

facts.label: Conversation-text export
facts.value: Retrieve Ticket List API documents paginated JSON with customer details, ticket properties, and a messages array containing plain-text message content, timestamps, sender/recipient, and reply-agent information.

facts.label: Export gaps
facts.value: Attachment binary export, separate complete customer-list download, internal-note coverage, all CSAT comments, article versions, and a single complete archive format were not published in checked export/API docs.

facts.label: Articles and related content
facts.value: Help articles are connected from the distinct Knowledge Base product; Desk integration does not document a complete article/comment/media export.

facts.label: Hosting region and AI providers
facts.value: Exact Desk hosting region/region-choice policy and named current AI providers were not published in the checked privacy, terms, GDPR page, and product sources.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Terms/GDPR page offer a DPA for qualifying paid customers on request; current subprocessor list is request-based through a form.

facts.label: AI privacy statement
facts.value: Privacy policy says personal data is not used to train third-party AI models; inputs/relevant account data may be processed by third-party AI providers, and de-identified/aggregated data may improve its own AI features.

facts.label: Free/trial content licence
facts.value: Terms section 27a grants a surviving licence over public and private free/trial user content, including AI/model training, product improvement, analytics, and other business purposes.

facts.label: Public content licence
facts.value: Publicly published content, including knowledge articles, may be retained indefinitely and used for service operation, search indexing, AI training, and business purposes; terms carve out identifiable personal data for AI training.

facts.label: Active history and free inactivity
facts.value: Pricing advertises unlimited ticket history. Terms say active free data may remain while active and for a reasonable recovery period; prolonged free inactivity is typically 12+ months, after which deletion or retention is discretionary.

facts.label: Paid cancellation and recovery
facts.value: Paid access continues until prepaid term ends, then account closes and members lose access. Private content kept 30 days for paid reactivation; after that may be deleted/not recoverable.

facts.label: Public deletion and residual retention
facts.value: Terms say delete public content before closing the account; otherwise it may remain indefinitely. Deleted content may remain in backups/caches; privacy retains information as needed for legal, business, or tax purposes.

facts.label: Exact purge and object recovery
facts.value: Backup purge days, per-ticket trash recovery period, source-embedding deletion time, AI-provider retention days, and precise complete erasure deadline were not published in the checked sources.

facts.label: Identity and lifecycle
facts.value: ProProfs Help Desk; active hosted help-desk product in the ProProfs family. No product-specific sunset, shutdown, or acquisition notice found in the checked sources.

facts.label: Company and country
facts.value: Terms contract with Batia Infotech, also called ProProfs; published address in Santa Monica, California, USA.

facts.label: Buying restrictions
facts.value: Terms exclude users subject to relevant US embargo/export restrictions and restricted-party lists; no complete Desk-specific country availability list found.

facts.label: Regional offers
facts.value: Public pricing code supports USD, AUD, BRL, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, SGD, and JPY, with geographic detection and a USD option for supported local currencies.

facts.label: Edition and licence
facts.value: Vendor-hosted proprietary service accessed through a browser; terms grant a limited, revocable, non-transferable use licence. No self-hosted core edition identified.

facts.label: Vendor support
facts.value: Essentials: email/live chat support. Business: chat/email/phone and 24/7 support claim. Elite: premium 24/7 support, dedicated account manager/technical officer and priority handling.

facts.label: Response promises and free support
facts.value: Guaranteed numerical response times, support time-zone specification, and exact free-plan staffed-hours entitlement were not published in the checked pricing/support/terms sources.

facts.label: Freshness
facts.value: Checked 2026-11-05; terms updated 2026-10-21; live AI source/generation guides and current public purchasing pages reviewed. Suggested next review 2026-12-05.

facts.label: Enterprise plan limits

facts.label: Free Cloud price
facts.value: $0/mo; no time limit; 1 seat.

facts.label: Pro Cloud price
facts.value: $29/mo equivalent, with $348 billed yearly; 5 seats included.

facts.label: Business Cloud price
facts.value: $59/mo equivalent, with $708 billed yearly; 20 seats included.

facts.label: Monthly-billed paid prices
facts.value: A Monthly selector is present, but the current page's accessible text does not expose the monthly-billing amounts. The older help article's per-seat monthly rates belong to a different plan structure and cannot be mapped to today's workspace plans.

facts.label: Currency and tax
facts.value: Prices are shown with $; the current pricing page and Terms checked do not identify the currency code or state whether tax is included.

facts.label: Current vs older Cloud price model
facts.value: Current Cloud pricing is Free / Pro / Business / Enterprise at fixed workspace prices with included seat caps. The older Cloud help article describes Free / Growth / Pro / Scale with per-seat rates. The pricing page is the current source.

facts.label: Cloud billing unit
facts.value: Current Cloud plans are billed per workspace and bundle a number of teammate seats; each workspace has its own plan, seat allowance, AI usage, and invoice. Pending team invites count toward seat caps.

facts.label: Customer usage unit
facts.value: Pricing says customers and conversations are unlimited on every Cloud plan; the public price page does not charge per support conversation or per customer.

facts.label: Email usage unit
facts.value: Cloud limits the monthly count of changelog, status, and notification emails by plan; sign-in emails are excluded.

facts.label: AI usage unit
facts.value: Current pricing expresses AI allowances as Basic, Standard, 5x Standard, or 20x Standard per workspace per month; usage resets monthly. No per-resolution fee is listed.

facts.label: Minimum purchase
facts.value: Free starts with 1 seat. Paid plans include 5 seats on Pro, 20 on Business, and unlimited on Enterprise; no separate paid seat add-on or paid seat minimum is listed on the current page.

facts.label: Contract and setup fees
facts.value: Annual prices are shown as yearly billed totals; monthly billing is offered via a selector, but the current monthly totals, setup fee, and minimum contract term are not stated in the accessible pricing text.

facts.label: Cloud AI plan allowance
facts.value: Free: Basic AI usage; Pro: Standard; Business: 5× Standard; Enterprise: 20× Standard. The current price matrix says allowances reset monthly.

facts.label: Cloud AI charge detail
facts.value: Current pricing lists no per-resolution fee and tells users to move up a plan for more included usage. An older AI billing article gives dollar allowances and $10 top-ups under the old Growth/Pro/Scale names; exact amounts cannot be assigned to current plans.

facts.label: Self-hosted AI provider
facts.value: Self-hosted AI is off until configured. The instance can use an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including a local model server; the operator supplies and pays for that provider or server.

facts.label: AI cost examples
facts.value: A reliable cost for 100 or 500 AI replies/resolutions cannot be calculated: the current Cloud page gives relative tiers but no current request/token allowance or per-unit price.

facts.label: Email overage
facts.value: Current pricing gives monthly email caps but does not state current overage or stop behavior. The older Cloud billing help page says a $10 pack buys 10,000 emails; because it uses the superseded plan model, applicability to current plans is unclear.

facts.label: AI overage
facts.value: Current pricing says AI usage resets monthly and advises moving up a plan when more is needed. It does not state whether use is hard-stopped or whether a current AI top-up can be purchased.

facts.label: Cancellation and downgrade
facts.value: Current page says a downgrade takes effect at the period end without deleting data; cancellation leaves the plan active until the period ends, after which the workspace moves to Free.

facts.label: Branding removal
facts.value: Paid plans can add removal of the “Powered by Quackback” badge from the portal, widget, help center, and status page: $59/mo or $590/year as displayed.

facts.label: Buying access
facts.value: Cloud is self-serve: a no-card Free plan and a no-card 14-day trial for each paid plan are offered. The pricing page describes Free as suitable for solo founders. Self-hosting is also publicly available.

facts.label: Type and fit
facts.value: Combined customer support inbox (website Messenger chat, email, and tickets), customer help center, feedback boards, roadmap, changelog, and status page. Classified here for support; feedback management is an overlap and directory boundary.

facts.label: Native customer channels
facts.value: Publicly documented support channels are website Messenger chat in the widget and email routed into the shared inbox; support tickets are also available in the portal.

facts.label: Channel limits
facts.value: Inbound email addresses: Free 1, Pro 1, Business 2, Enterprise unlimited. Widget Messenger is included on all Cloud plans; no separate chat charge is listed.

facts.label: Other support channels
facts.value: The pricing, support-channel, and integration pages checked do not document native WhatsApp, SMS, Instagram/Messenger social inbox, or voice support channels.

facts.label: Assignment and private notes
facts.value: Inbox supports assignment to an individual or team, bulk assignment, priority, internal notes, mentions, and views for Mine, Unassigned, All, and Mentions.

facts.label: Conversation controls
facts.value: Agents can search message content and visitor name, set priority, snooze, close/reopen, and use macros. The checked pages do not describe a real-time collision warning.

facts.label: Macros, routing, and workflows
facts.value: Macros can send a saved reply with assignment, team, tag, priority, snooze, or close actions. Business has teams/routing, SLAs, and 10 active workflows; Enterprise has unlimited active workflows.

facts.label: Office hours and SLAs
facts.value: Business and Enterprise include SLA policies. Office hours use a chosen time zone and can pause human SLA timers outside working intervals; workflows apply policies and can route breach events.

facts.label: Workspaces and brands
facts.value: Each workspace has its own plan, seat allowance, AI usage, and invoice. The exact maximum number of workspaces per Cloud account is not published on the current pricing page.

facts.label: Support addresses and domain
facts.value: Inbound email addresses are capped by plan (F17). Custom domain is included from Pro in the current pricing matrix. Self-hosting uses the operator's own domain and BASE_URL.

facts.label: Help center
facts.value: Searchable public help-center articles and categories are included across Cloud plans and can also be shown inside the widget. The page separates the help center from the support inbox module.

facts.label: Article and language limits
facts.value: Current pricing does not list a help-article count limit. Cloud help-center language caps are Free 1, Pro 1, Business 3, Enterprise unlimited.

facts.label: Help-center custom domain
facts.value: The official guide describes a workspace help hostname and a customer-owned CNAME domain; Cloud custom domains start at the older Growth tier in that guide, while current pricing places the feature on Pro and above.

facts.label: AI roles
facts.value: Quinn has a customer-facing Agent in Messenger and a teammate-facing Copilot for answers and draft replies. Free lists Copilot drafts; the customer Agent and Copilot answers start on Pro.

facts.label: AI analytics
facts.value: Current pricing includes AI insights, duplicates, and post summaries on paid plans; the product documentation describes automatic summaries, duplicate suggestions, and Quinn analytics.

facts.label: AI knowledge sources
facts.value: The newest Privacy help article (updated 1 day before this check) says Agent sources include help articles, public posts, changelog, documents, and status; Copilot can additionally use past conversations, internal notes, and tickets. Two older AI docs omit documents from the Agent list.

facts.label: Source freshness and citations
facts.value: Most knowledge sources are retrieval-indexed; service status is looked up live. The docs do not publish a fixed indexing schedule or promise that every answer includes a source citation.

facts.label: Human fallback
facts.value: Quinn can hand the live conversation to a human in the same support workflow. The handoff can trigger a workflow/webhook and notify a teammate or team. Human response outside office hours depends on the team's schedule; Quinn remains available around the clock.

facts.label: Customer actions
facts.value: Built-in Quinn actions include searching published knowledge, checking live status, handing off, recording attributes, closing a confirmed-resolved conversation, creating a ticket, and creating/sharing feedback posts. Admin can set each action to Allow, Ask for approval, or Never.

facts.label: Identity and approval
facts.value: Widget identity uses a server-signed SSO token; unsigned browser-supplied identity details are rejected in current docs. Write actions can require a teammate's approval; Copilot write actions require teammate approval before a change.

facts.label: Integrations
facts.value: Official integration pages list issue trackers (including Linear, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps), chat/alerts (Slack, Teams, Discord, ntfy), support/CRM tools (Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe), Segment, Zapier, Make, n8n, and webhooks.

facts.label: Relevant connector pricing
facts.value: Business and Enterprise include integrations on Cloud. Pro includes webhooks and the MCP server; the REST API has its own plan request caps. Self-hosted includes every integration without Quackback software fees.

facts.label: REST API
facts.value: API docs cover feedback, changelog, help center, conversations, tickets, status, users, and more. The current price matrix lists monthly request caps of 10K for Free/Pro, 250K for Business, and 2M for Enterprise; an export feature page says REST API read/write is Pro and up, leaving Free API scope unclear.

facts.label: Webhooks and MCP
facts.value: Pro and above include webhooks and an MCP server. Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256, retry selected failures up to 3 times, and can cover support events; MCP can read and respond to support conversations when enabled.

facts.label: Widget libraries
facts.value: Web widget uses an asynchronous JavaScript SDK; official iOS and Android SDKs wrap it for native apps. The docs require server-signed identity for production users.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Official minimum: 1 CPU core, 1 GB RAM, 10 GB storage; PostgreSQL 14+ with pgvector 0.5.0+ and pg_trgm. Docker Compose bundles PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage; Docker Engine 20.10+ and Compose v2+ are documented.

facts.label: Self-host install paths
facts.value: Docker Compose is the recommended production path; Docker run, Railway, and manual deployment are also documented. Published container images support linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

facts.label: Operator duties
facts.value: Self-hosted operators handle infrastructure, domain/TLS, security, backups, upgrades, monitoring, storage, and email delivery. Upgrades require a backup; v0.13 to v0.14 needs a one-time migration and does not support downgrade without restoring a backup.

facts.label: Self-host module and provider costs
facts.value: The complete product has no Quackback seat or feature licence fees under AGPL-3.0. Hosting, email delivery, optional object storage, and any external AI provider/server are separately supplied and priced by the operator.

facts.label: Widget languages
facts.value: The widget documents English, French, German, Spanish, and Arabic with right-to-left layout; it auto-detects browser language or accepts a locale override.

facts.label: Help center and agent UI languages
facts.value: Help-center capacity is 1 language on Free/Pro, 3 on Business, and unlimited on Enterprise. A complete agent-dashboard UI language list was not found in the widget, pricing, or help-center localization pages checked.

facts.label: Agent platform
facts.value: A browser-based Admin workspace is documented. The pricing, support, mobile SDK, and self-hosting pages checked did not list a native agent desktop download or dedicated agent mobile app.

facts.label: Customer platform needs
facts.value: No host CMS or ecommerce platform is required for the web widget: it is installed by adding a JavaScript snippet. Official iOS and Android SDKs are available for customer-facing in-app use.

facts.label: Reporting
facts.value: Current Cloud pricing lists cross-product analytics for feedback, support, CSAT, AI, and changelog on all plans; CSV analytics exports start on Business. Enterprise adds visitor analytics.

facts.label: AI reporting and surveys
facts.value: Quinn analytics include resolutions, handoffs, action outcomes, and Copilot use; conversation CSAT can be requested after close. No response-time benchmark formula beyond documented SLA targets was found in the checked reporting pages.

facts.label: Workspace export
facts.value: Business, Enterprise, and self-hosted editions can export the workspace as a ZIP: boards, posts, comments, votes, users, companies, changelog, and help articles as CSV; conversations and internal notes as JSON Lines. Download links expire after 7 days per help docs.

facts.label: Conversation transcript export
facts.value: Any conversation or ticket can be saved as a Markdown transcript. The current marketing export page identifies support conversations, messages, and internal notes in the workspace export.

facts.label: Export limitations
facts.value: The documented full ZIP excludes any explicit guarantee about attachment export; the API offers another route, with current per-plan rate caps.

facts.label: Hosted data location
facts.value: Privacy says Cloudflare provides hosting and content delivery, but no hosting country/region or customer-selectable region was published.

facts.label: Hosted subprocessors
facts.value: The legal Privacy page names Cloudflare for hosting/CDN, Google Analytics for anonymised usage analytics, and Resend for transactional email. No detailed current subprocessor list or DPA was found.

facts.label: AI data handling and training
facts.value: Current help privacy says Cloud AI is run by Quackback but does not name the Cloud model provider or state a model-training/retention policy. Self-hosted content goes only to the configured endpoint; enabled features send their required input content.

facts.label: Self-host telemetry
facts.value: A self-hosted instance sends an anonymous daily usage snapshot by default with a random instance ID, version/platform, enabled modules/integrations, and banded counts; it excludes names, emails, URLs, hostnames, and content. It can be disabled.

facts.label: Cloud retention and deletion
facts.value: Legal Privacy says hosted data is retained while the account is active and personal data is removed within 30 days of account deletion; anonymised aggregate analytics may remain.

facts.label: Portal user deletion and content

facts.label: Volume stop/extra bill uncertainty

facts.label: Widget and help-site branding removal
facts.value: Exact permission, minimum plan and fee for removing vendor attribution from the chat widget or FAQ were not established.

facts.label: Outgoing-email appearance

facts.label: Type and fit
facts.value: Our classification: shared support inbox with email, web chat, social channels, FAQ and ecommerce context; overlaps knowledge bases, customer messaging and AI support agents.

facts.label: Email
facts.value: Native email channels on Basic and above, and Starter via Basic features; unlimited inboxes. Forward an existing address or use the assigned Re:amaze address.

facts.label: Website and web-app chat
facts.value: Native Reamaze.js Shoutbox/Lightbox, two-way messaging and inline contact surfaces. Basic includes chat; synchronous Classic Chat mode requires Plus.

facts.label: Native customer mobile chat
facts.value: Official customer iOS/Android SDKs currently support a knowledge-base embed only; native chat is not documented in that SDK scope.

facts.label: Messenger / Facebook
facts.value: Native connected Facebook Page/Messenger channel imports comments, messages, reviews, mentions and lead ads. Social channels included on Basic and higher/Starter.

facts.label: Instagram
facts.value: Native comments/mentions connection and separate DMs channel for Business accounts. Can receive/reply to DMs and story mentions.

facts.label: WhatsApp
facts.value: Native connected WhatsApp Business channel through Twilio; needs Twilio account and WhatsApp-enabled number.

facts.label: SMS/MMS
facts.value: Native provider connections for Twilio, ClickSend, RingCentral and SMSBump; Pro/Plus per pricing. Custom SMS channel also documented.

facts.label: Voice and video
facts.value: Pro/Plus voice-provider integrations: Aircall, RingCentral, AT&T Office@Hand, JustCall. Plus adds in-chat video calls.

facts.label: Slack and Discord
facts.value: Slack integration delivers inbox event notifications and staff mentions. Native two-way customer Slack inbox and Discord channel were not established.

facts.label: Contact forms
facts.value: Native inline contact form, routing to a chosen support channel and supporting attachments/custom fields.

facts.label: X / Twitter
facts.value: Old shared Twitter integration was sunset; replacement uses the customer's own paid X developer app/project.

facts.label: Teamwork and collision control
facts.value: Assignment, internal notes, @/recipient notifications, saved replies, presence and workflow routing. If two staff replies occur within 5 minutes, the second is held for review and can be deliberately published.

facts.label: Workflows and office hours
facts.value: Automated/manual workflows can assign, tag, reply, add notes and route conversations. Brand office hours and blackout dates affect availability messages, autoresponders and staff response-time calculations.

facts.label: Brands and inboxes
facts.value: Basic one brand; Pro/Plus unlimited brands. Email inboxes and social channels are listed unlimited on the three user plans. Starter inherits Basic's one-brand feature set.

facts.label: Multiple sites and separation
facts.value: Multiple independent stores/businesses can be managed in one account using separate brands. Staff access can be restricted by brand; each brand has one FAQ configuration.

facts.label: FAQ deployment and visibility
facts.value: Native public/internal/draft FAQ articles, topics and search. Deploy as a vendor-hosted Help Site, inline website embed or widget FAQ. Each brand has its FAQ.

facts.label: Custom FAQ domain
facts.value: Pro/Plus can use a custom domain; CNAME points to reamaze.lida.clearalias.com. Default Help Site uses a Re:amaze domain.

facts.label: Article feedback and history
facts.value: Plus includes Article Feedback and FAQ Article Edit History.

facts.label: Article limits and translation
facts.value: Numeric article/storage caps and automatic parallel article translations were not established.

facts.label: AI Agent role and channels
facts.value: Autonomous AI Agent handles chat, email and SMS using enabled knowledge sources. Enable selected channels/brands; AI replies mark threads Responded rather than automatically Done.

facts.label: Staff AI tools
facts.value: Suggested/improved replies, quick responses, conversation summaries, sentiment, incoming-message translation and FAQ/template generation.

facts.label: AI knowledge and instructions
facts.value: FAQ, response templates, custom AI context, external URLs and connected Shopify/WooCommerce product/order data. Choose sources to include/exclude; per-brand personality and response guidelines.

facts.label: External-URL limit conflict
facts.value: Custom AI settings guide says up to 5 single-page URLs for AI FAQ bot. Dedicated current AI Agent URL guide says up to 20 in the same Custom AI Context setting.

facts.label: URL refresh and source visibility
facts.value: AI Agent periodically re-scrapes supplied public pages, one page per URL, no link-following/site-wide crawl. Staff can inspect a source count/list on each AI reply and open source types.

facts.label: Corrections and approved learning
facts.value: Up to 100 saved AI corrections; Improve Response is available when an FAQ article was used. Learned Answers require staff approval, maximum 50 saved; unapproved suggestions expire after 14 days.

facts.label: Escalation
facts.value: AI Agent escalates when it cannot answer; guidelines say escalation for upset customers is built in. Escalated conversations are not AI billable resolutions.

facts.label: Handoff controls and offline continuation
facts.value: Exact customer “speak to a person” control, configurable AI handoff destination and a formal transcript-transfer guarantee were not established. Normal chat stores conversations in an associated email channel and can deliver later replies by email.

facts.label: Human payment/order actions
facts.value: Staff can refund/cancel subscriptions in Stripe using matching customer email; WooCommerce module can refund, update order/payment status and add notes.

facts.label: Customer identity and AI-action limits

facts.label: Ecommerce connections
facts.value: Shopify and WooCommerce integrations provide store/order context. WooCommerce module matches customer email and supports order actions; Shopify connection is optional for non-store users.

facts.label: Payments, issue tracking and automation

facts.value: Native Linear/Discord integrations were not established.

facts.label: SDKs, custom modules and webhooks
facts.value: Reamaze.js embeds, knowledge-base-only mobile SDKs and custom module SDK. Custom SMS uses signed incoming requests and a configured outgoing webhook for staff replies.

facts.label: Agent devices and platform
facts.value: Modern web browser plus native iOS/Android staff apps. Mobile apps support inbox handling, notes, assignment, workflows and integration context.

facts.label: Customer libraries and embedding
facts.value: Web SDK for sites/web apps; separate iOS/Android SDKs limited to KB embedding; custom module SDK can place the buyer's own UI/data/actions beside a support conversation.

facts.label: Support reports
facts.value: Basic: volume, channels, response time, first-response resolve rate and thread size. Pro adds advanced reports; Plus adds staff summary/individual reports.

facts.label: Satisfaction plan scope
facts.value: Pricing lists customer satisfaction ratings on Plus; reporting overview lists the Satisfaction Ratings Report on Pro. Whether Pro can configure/collect the same surveys was not resolved.

facts.label: AI reporting and review
facts.value: AI/Chatbot and AI Productivity reports cover involvement, session outcomes/escalations, usage and successful AI API requests. Test Agent shows Answered/Escalated/Resolved/Failed and sources.

facts.label: Contacts
facts.value: Native filtered/all-contact CSV export runs in background and emails when ready. Contacts API returns account-wide contacts and supports pagination/filtering.

facts.label: Conversation text and notes
facts.value: JSON conversation list/detail and message APIs; retrieve messages globally or within a thread. Message response includes body, timestamps, authors, visibility and optional original HTML.

facts.label: Attachments
facts.value: Message API includes attachment file name, content type, size, thumbnail URL and file URL.

facts.label: FAQ and satisfaction feedback
facts.value: Articles API returns article body, topic, status and timestamps; defaults to published, with draft/internal filters. Satisfaction API returns numeric rating and optional comment with customer/staff/conversation IDs.

facts.label: Complete one-click archive
facts.value: A complete self-service archive combining conversation text, binaries, all FAQ states and all feedback was not found.

facts.label: Infrastructure and subprocessors

facts.label: Storage region choice
facts.value: Exact Re:amaze account data-center regions and a buyer-selectable residency option were not established.

facts.value: Incorporated GoDaddy AI terms permit using AI input/output to operate and improve services. Re:amaze DPA limits Customer Personal Data processing to service purposes/instructions. A blanket no-model-training/no-retention promise was not established.

facts.value: Subscription may be suspended unpaid/read-only for up to 6 months; no replies, but data remains accessible. After 6 months information/configuration is deleted. Owner can instead close the account and permanently delete account data.

facts.value: Terms say cancellation takes effect immediately, no unused-time refund, and data removal is irreversible; they reserve retaining non-restorable copies. DPA allows return/deletion/de-identification and legally required retention after termination.

facts.value: Fixed active-history cap, inactivity-only deletion rule, post-trial access window and backup-erasure timetable were not established.
